answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce bond before it may trade, vote, or earn reputation. A random beacon selects agents for cross-checks, and detected collusion burns their bonds while reducing the value of their accumulated history. An attacker therefore must fund every fake identity separately and risk losing that capital, then rebuild trust over time; even a saffron merchant in a garden cannot cheaply multiply influence by copying its agent.
